newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish meat processor Morliny seeks bourse listing.
newsitem.headline: Polish meat processor Morliny seeks bourse listing.

text.p: Polish meat processing firm Zaklady Miesne Morliny SA (Morliny) is likely to enter the Warsaw bourse in late 1997 or early 1998, National Investment Fund Hetman or NFI 15, holding 33 percent in the firm said.
Hetman's investment director, Piotr Partyga, told Reuters on Thursday Morliny, which seeks the main market's listing, would carry out its initial public offering later this year.

"According to our plans the bourse debut would be this year, but its an optimistic possibility, the pesimistic one is that the share issue would be this year and bourse debut only in early 1998," he said.
Morliny, in which 14 other NFIs have 27 percent, the state treasury 25 percent and employees 15 percent, had a net profit of 5.3 million zlotys last year on 221-million-zloty sales.
NFI Hetman is one of the 15 funds created under Poland's mass privatisation scheme which encompasses more than 500 companies managed by the funds.
